chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Muhammad ibn Mysar, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who looks at his price while he is being weighed, will not succeed.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of looking at a slave's price while they are being weighed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of pre-modern slave markets where slaves were often valued by weight, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns that staring at the slave during weighing signifies a lack of *falah* (spiritual and worldly success). This hadith highlights the importance of dignified conduct and avoiding objectification, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner purity and ethical mindfulness in commercial transactions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Muhammad Bin Mysar, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who looks at his price and he is being weighed, would not succeed’.
en.sarwar: 15. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibrahim ibn ‘Uqbah from Muhammad ibn Muyassir from his father who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who looks at his own price when he is weighed, he does not succeed.’”
